violated_contract: A provider's static capability table is part of the call contract. A target the provider can never serve must be filtered before dispatch: rediscovering the same permanent rejection as a 4xx on every call burns a round trip per batch forever, and because the rejection is client input, counting it in the provider's error-budget ratios pages on a perfectly healthy service.
canonical_prevention: Mirror the provider's supported-target table on the caller side (one shared set, with a test pinning parity against the provider's own table), check the session target before queueing dispatch, and count the skip on a bounded metric with one log per session. Provider-agnostic lanes that serve every target stay exempt. Alert error-ratio rules must exclude client-input rejection statuses from the numerator, the denominator, and the volume gate so the budget measures service failures over service-eligible requests.
